methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 878 patients with one 80:20 split (randomly chosen from 10 candidate splits, which is unusual and not a true cross-validation). Deep features extracted from pretrained DenseNet201 on 2D frames only, with tumor segmentation on the largest cross-section rather than volumetric data. Feature-selection pipeline (Mann-Whitney, Spearman, LASSO) retains 76-101 features for training set outcomes yet the training-to-test AUC gap is enormous (TDUS 0.935 to 0.586; CDUS 0.805 to 0.521; CEUS 0.950 to 0.740), indicating severe overfitting that the authors partially acknowledge but which invalidates several of their quantitative claims. Outcome definition (distant metastasis) relies on cross-sectional imaging without histopathological confirmation, as acknowledged. No external validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective diagnostic/prediction cohort maps to LoE 2b. The potential to screen for distant metastasis via TRUS-based radiomics would be clinically attractive (low cost, no radiation) but test-set AUC of 0.740 with PPV of 0.286 and a nomogram based on only platelet count, alcohol, and a CEUS radiomics score is far from clinically deployable; staging-relevant variables (TNM, CEA, EMVI) are absent.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the appropriate standard for a prediction model. The paper reports participants, outcome adjudication (dual-sonographer with tiebreaker), predictor extraction pipeline, feature-selection procedures, ICC for segmentation (0.91-0.94), and AUC plus secondary metrics with a nomogram. Missing TRIPOD items: sample size justification, missing-data handling, calibration plots or Brier scores, model coefficients or full LR equations, decision-curve analysis, and an external validation cohort. No data/code availability, no published model weights, and no checklist.

novelty_literature.justification: This is presented as the first CETRUS-based deep learning radiomics model for distant-metastasis prediction in rectal cancer; CT/MRI radiomics work on the same question exists (Li 2020, Liu 2021). The modality extension to transrectal ultrasound is genuinely new, but the methodology (DenseNet201 feature extraction + LR) is standard, and the modest test-set performance limits the meaningful novel contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized conventionally and reasonably clear. Figures and tables are appropriately referenced. Issues include grammatical roughness in places, redundant sentences (the repeated 'showed promising predictive performance' language across Abstract, Discussion, and Conclusions), and the Conclusions section is nearly verbatim from the end of the Abstract. The limitations paragraph is genuinely thoughtful about imaging-only metastasis definition and short follow-up.

key_strengths: Novel application of deep learning radiomics on contrast-enhanced transrectal ultrasound (CETRUS) in a substantial 878-patient cohort
Clearly described feature extraction pipeline using DenseNet201 with sequential Mann-Whitney/Spearman/LASSO feature selection
Dual-reader outcome adjudication with tiebreaker for both CT and liver CEUS, plus explicit ICC reporting for ROI segmentation
Honest limitations paragraph addressing imaging-only metastasis definition and lack of external validation
key_concerns: Severe training-to-test AUC gaps (TDUS 0.935->0.586; CDUS 0.805->0.521; CEUS 0.950->0.740) indicate pronounced overfitting that undermines most performance claims
Clinical model uses only alcohol consumption and platelet count; standard rectal-cancer staging variables (TNM, CEA, EMVI, MRF status) are absent
Distant metastasis defined on imaging without histopathology; follow-up duration not quantified
Single 80:20 split chosen from 10 candidates rather than proper k-fold cross-validation or external validation cohort
No calibration plot, no decision-curve analysis, no TRIPOD checklist, no model weights or code released
Low PPV (0.286 in test set) makes the nomogram impractical for clinical deployment as presented
chief_reviewer.rationale: A novel imaging modality application with substantial overfitting, a weak clinical feature set, and imaging-only outcome adjudication; suitable for a lower-tier specialty journal only after major revisions incorporating external validation, calibration analysis, and additional clinical predictors.
